settings.what: The hand bag, for the open sun

settings.title: Nizhal
settings.what: The shoulder bag, for the slow hours

settings.title: Maalai
settings.what: The tote, for when people arrive

settings.title: Vizha
settings.what: Two clutches, for the nights kept back

settings.name: Veyil
settings.text: A circle cut clean through leather, the weave burning through the opening.
settings.alt: Veyil hand bag held by its circular cut-out handle: tan leather around crimson and natural striped paai

settings.title: Veyil
settings.text:
Every household keeps a katta pai by the door — the one grabbed without thinking, on the way out for a market run.

Folded under an arm, bright enough to be picked out from the end of the street. Veyil keeps that brightness, and that way of being carried: the same readiness, made for the open sun.
settings.scene_alt: Morning sun rippling across an ochre wall with a small shuttered window
settings.scene_2_alt: A lattice window set in a sunlit ochre wall
settings.caption: The market run

settings.text: By afternoon the light has moved.

settings.name: Nizhal
settings.text: The chequer of the tiled floor, taken onto the shoulder — long, low and unhurried, the way the hour is.
settings.alt: Nizhal shoulder baguette tucked under an arm: navy, rust and natural chequered paai with a tan leather strap

settings.title: Nizhal
settings.text:
There’s a particular kind of afternoon — too warm to be outside, quiet enough that the tiles hold the light in patches.

It comes through the grill and lies across the floor in squares, and the house goes quiet behind it. Nizhal is that pause: structured, close, unhurried. The shape of an afternoon, slow.
settings.scene_alt: The shadow of a woman crossing a patch of afternoon light on a wall
settings.scene_2_alt: The shadow of leaves falling across a pale wall
settings.caption: The tiles, holding the light

settings.text: Then the mat is unrolled, and people arrive.

settings.name: Maalai
settings.text: Black and beige — the paai in its oldest colouring, the one nobody thinks to call a pattern.
settings.alt: Maalai domed tote: black and natural striped paai with black leather straps and base

settings.title: Maalai
settings.text:
A paai, laid out flat, holds an entire gathering — from food and conversation to people settling in around it.

Maalai carries that same instinct into a tote: wide and unfussy, made to hold whatever a day brings into it. Not only evenings, but just everything.
settings.scene_alt: Low evening sun breaking through the branches of an old tree
settings.scene_2_alt: A cup of tea and a plate of fritters, seen from above
settings.caption: When people come

settings.name: Long Clutch
settings.text: One length of paai runs unbroken across the back, over the flap and down the front — a single piece, folded rather than joined.
settings.alt: Vizha long clutch held against the hip: wine and natural paai bound in aubergine leather

settings.name: Half Moon
settings.text: The weave rises on both sides of a leather handle and meets at the top: a mat folded once, and carried by the fold.
settings.alt: Vizha half-moon clutch on a ledge: magenta and emerald paai with a tan leather handle

settings.title: Vizha
settings.text:
Some colours are kept back. They are not for the floor or the afternoon; they come out of the cupboard for weddings, for temple nights, for the days a house fills up.

Vizha is woven in those — jewelled greens, magentas, wine — in two pieces made to be held rather than worn.
settings.scene_alt: A fountain of golden sparks from a festival firework at night
settings.scene_2_alt: Gold bangles stacked in a shop, close
settings.caption: The night worth dressing for

settings.title: Split
settings.text: Korai grass, split by hand into fine strands.

settings.title: Soaked
settings.text: Left in water until it softens enough to take the loom.

settings.title: Dyed
settings.text: In the colours each hour of the day asks for.

settings.title: Woven
settings.text: Worked wet, thread by thread, until the mat folds like cloth.
